belongs_to: Let Us Think Q1: "The given shapes stand for numbers between 1 and 24. The same shape denotes the same number across all problems. Find the numbers hiding in all the shapes."
description: Six shape equations in two columns of three, labelled a) to f) (a, b, c down the left column; d, e, f down the right column). Each shape is a flat coloured shape with a thin dark outline, with a × sign between the factors and an = sign before the result. Shapes used: BLUE rectangle (wide, about 2:1, cornflower blue); PINK circle; LILAC (light purple) triangle (isosceles, point up); ORANGE diamond (rhombus standing on a corner); GREEN pentagon (regular, point up); YELLOW (pale yellow) parallelogram leaning to the right; LIGHT-BLUE half-disc (semicircle tilted so that its straight edge slopes; curved side on the left); WHITE (unfilled, outline only) notched shape = a tall central rectangle with a small rectangular tab sticking out at the middle of its left side and the same tab at the middle of its right side (a plus-like block with short arms). a) blue rectangle × pink circle = lilac triangle. b) blue rectangle × blue rectangle (the same blue rectangle twice) = white notched shape. c) yellow parallelogram × orange diamond = lilac triangle. d) orange diamond × green pentagon = orange diamond. e) yellow parallelogram × pink circle = light-blue half-disc. f) light-blue half-disc × blue rectangle = yellow parallelogram × lilac triangle (shapes on BOTH sides of the = sign). No number is printed anywhere in the figure; the same colour+shape means the same number in all six lines.
unclear: Exact proportions of the shapes (e.g. rectangle width:height) are approximate; the identity of every shape and colour is certain.
